newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: North Korea seeks to join ADB.
newsitem.headline: North Korea seeks to join ADB.

text.p: North Korea wants to join the Asian Development Bank (ADB) and the bank's member-nations will be formally informed of its request shortly, a top ADB official said on Monday.
"North Korea has expressed strong interest in joining this institution and we are now in a position to tell existing members of the request," ADB president Mitsuo Sato told Reuters in an interview.
The Manila-based financial institution which is owned by 56 countries was formed 30 years ago to help steer Asia's economic development.
Besides lending on commercial terms, the bank grants soft loans to the poorest countries in the region.
North Korea's request would be passed on to the ADB's 12 board directors who would in turn inform the member countries.

Sato said North Korea's admission to the bank would depend on how many members supported it. Member-nations had not expressed their views on the subject since they had not yet been formally told of North Korea's request, he said.
If the request was favourably received the ADB could start negotiating the terms of entry.
To become a member Pyongyang would be expected to contribute to the bank's capital.
North Korea officially applied for membership of the Manila-based institution in 1992, but the bank decided its entry bid was premature.
Communist North Korea, which has isolated itself from the rest of the world, is in economic crisis and much of its population are believed to be facing starvation.
